Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 16:20:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery Recap & Next Steps — Data Privacy and Logging Requirements

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so we have alignment and clear next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you shared:
- Current vendor logs raw user inputs and retention is unclear — legal is concerned about PII retention and auditability.
- Need ability to redact or prevent storage of PII at the inference layer.
- Lack of fine-grained audit logs for admin access to logs and model inputs.
- Cost/latency trade-offs: want sub-100ms median latency for user-facing queries, with predictable throughput for peak hours.

Current stack (from the call):
- Frontend > internal API layer (node) > in-house embedding/LLM routing service (hosts models on GCP us-west)
- Data classification: sensitive/PII flagged before sending to models in some flows, but not consistently enforced for legacy endpoints.

Success criteria for a POC we discussed:
1) Demonstrate that Redwood can be configured to avoid persisting raw PII to logs (either by real-time redaction or never logging raw inputs).
2) Provide audit logs showing who accessed inference logs and when (immutable export for up to 90 days).
3) Configurable retention policy with on-demand purge and a max default retention of 30 days for request-level logs; ability to extend for operational logs if needed.
4) Meet latency target (median <100ms for our test workload) and maintain reasonable cost per 1k queries.

Privacy/logging constraints called out by legal/security:
- PII must be redacted or never persist beyond 24 hours unless explicitly approved.
- Any stored request/response logs must be encrypted at rest and access-controlled with KMS.
- Customer needs point-in-time ability to delete logs (right-to-be-forgotten) and an auditable purge trail.
- Need SOC 2 evidence and a list of what is written to disk in the default flow.

Attachments I’ll share with this email (below):
- redwood-soc2-overview.pdf (SOC 2 scope & controls summary)
- redwood-data-retention-template.docx (example retention policy + purge workflow)

Next steps (action owners & timing):
- Redwood (Marissa): share SOC2 summary + data retention template (attached) — today.
- Redwood (Rishi): schedule a 60-min security deep-dive to walk logging controls + redaction options — propose Mon/Tue windows below.
- Acme (Alex/Priya): confirm retention baseline (30 vs 90 days) and whether on-demand purge API is required. Also share sample non-production payloads (PII redacted) for performance testing.

Proposed times for security deep-dive (Pacific): Mon 2026-02-16 10:00 or Tue 2026-02-17 09:00 — Rishi, please flag availability.

Thanks — looking forward to the next step.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmecorp.com>

Cc: Priya Suresh <priya.suresh@acmecorp.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap & Next Steps — Data Privacy and Logging Requirements

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary and aligns with our notes. A couple clarifications: 

- Retention: for operational troubleshooting logs we typically keep up to 90 days, but for request-level logs containing any PII we require automatic redaction within 24 hours and the ability to purge on-demand. Legal will likely push for the 24-hour hard requirement for PII-containing inputs.
- Auditability: we need immutable access logs for any admin access to logs (who, when, reason). That export should be pullable to our SIEM (we use Splunk).
- Data residency: all production logs and keys must remain in US regions for now.

I’m attaching our internal data-classification snippet so you can see how we mark PII in sample payloads.

We’re happy to do a POC — we can provide a redacted sample dataset (non-prod) and a smaller production traffic window for load testing.

Next — Mon 2026-02-16 10:00 PT works for a security deep-dive. Please send calendar invite.

Thanks,
Alex
Sr. Product Manager, Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acmecorp.com | +1 (212) 555-0987

Alex — perfect, thanks for the quick sync and for confirming Mon 2/16 at 10:00 PT. Calendar invite coming shortly.

A few notes ahead of the call so Rishi can prepare:
- Redaction options we’ll demo: client-side redaction (recommended), proxy-level redaction, and runtime filtering that prevents writes to persistent logs. We’ll show trade-offs and configuration examples.
- Audit logs: we can stream admin-access events to your SIEM (Splunk) and generate immutable export files for compliance.
- Retention/purge: our platform supports policy-driven retention per-tenant and on-demand purge APIs. We will note the default of 30 days for request-level logs and explain how to configure 90 days for operational logs if needed. You will have an auditable purge record.

Prep items for Acme before the security deep-dive:
- Share a redacted sample payload or describe data fields considered PII (this helps Rishi scope redaction rules).
- Confirm whether encrypted KMS keys must be customer-managed (bring-your-own-key).

I’ve attached the SOC2 summary and a retention template for your security team to review.

Thanks — Rishi / Priyom, would you please confirm availability for the times below and anything else we should bring?

Best,
Marissa
